![](2026/brauss.jpg)

Not the greatest month, hence the relative-silence on logical matters. And hence it wasn't possible to get to London to attend Elisabeth Brauß's lunchtime concert in the Wigmore Hall Autumn International Piano Festival at Wigmore Hall on Monday. But -- a delight -- the concert was broadcast live on BBC Sounds.

Elisabeth began with her beloved Mozart, this time the Piano Sonata in F, K332. Next she played numbers II to VI of Bartók's 14 Bagatelles Op. 6, and then XV Le baiser de l’Enfant-Jésus from Messaien's Vingt regards sur l’Enfant-Jésus (the Bartók and Messaien were all new to me, and I was much taken). 

There followed Chopin's Fantasy in F minor Op. 49. Beautifully played of course, but not a piece particularly to my taste. Perhaps as I listen again (and again?) Elisabeth will convince me -- very happily, we can [download the concert for a month](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/m0031pyj)

At the end of the live broadcast at 57.39, I was then completely poleaxed by her encore ... if I'd been in the hall would I have held it together ...?
